scope: Complete numbered reports 44–58, finishing the 51 numbered reports in this selected Book of Faith source. Ten provisional chapter headings; introductions remain separately preserved in Arabic. Independent review remains pending.

segments.arabic: [44] حدثنا مسلم بن إبراهيم قال: حدثنا هشام قال: حدثنا قتادة عن أنس عن النبي ﷺ قال:
segments.english: Muslim ibn Ibrahim related to us. He said: Hisham related to us. He said: Qatadah related to us, from Anas, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, who said:

segments.arabic: يخرج من النار من قال لا إله إلا الله وفي قلبه وزن شعيرة من خير ويخرج من النار من قال لا إله إلا الله وفي قلبه وزن برة من خير ويخرج من النار من قال لا إله إلا الله وفي قلبه وزن ذرة من خير
segments.english: “Whoever says ‘There is no god but Allah’ and has a barley grain’s weight of good in his heart will come out of the Fire. Whoever says ‘There is no god but Allah’ and has a wheat grain’s weight of good in his heart will come out of the Fire. Whoever says ‘There is no god but Allah’ and has a tiny particle’s weight of good in his heart will come out of the Fire.”

segments.arabic: قال أبو عبد الله قال أبان حدثنا قتادة حدثنا أنس عن النبي ﷺ من إيمان مكان من خير.
segments.english: Abu ‘Abdullah said: Aban said: Qatadah related to us. Anas related to us, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: “of faith” in place of “of good.”

notes: All three repeated declarations and weights remain in order: barley grain, wheat grain and dharrah, provisionally a tiny particle. The final Abu ‘Abdullah/Aban/Qatadah/Anas note is retained with its explicit substitution of faith for good.
Bewley abbreviates the closing note; the Khan-family report omits it. Neither abridgement replaces the selected full Arabic transmission. Both printed Arabic witnesses retain the note.

segments.arabic: [45] حدثنا الحسن بن الصباح سمع جعفر بن عون حدثنا أبو العميس أخبرنا قيس بن مسلم عن طارق بن شهاب عن عمر بن الخطاب:
segments.english: Al-Hasan ibn al-Sabbah related to us; he heard Ja‘far ibn ‘Awn: Abu al-‘Umays related to us. Qays ibn Muslim informed us, from Tariq ibn Shihab, from ‘Umar ibn al-Khattab:

segments.arabic: أن رجلا من اليهود قال له يا أمير المؤمنين آية في كتابكم تقرؤونها لو علينا معشر اليهود نزلت لاتخذنا ذلك اليوم عيدا قال أي آية قال { اليوم أكملت لكم دينكم وأتممت عليكم نعمتي ورضيت لكم الإسلام دينا } قال عمر قد عرفنا ذلك اليوم والمكان الذي نزلت فيه على النبي ﷺ وهو قائم بعرفة يوم جمعة
segments.english: A Jewish man said to him: “Commander of the Believers, there is a verse in your book that you recite. Had it been sent down to us Jews, we would have made that day a festival.” He said: “Which verse?” He said: {Today I have perfected your religion for you, completed My favour upon you, and approved Islam for you as a religion}. ‘Umar said: “We know that day and the place where it was sent down to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: he was standing at ‘Arafah on a Friday.”

notes: The opening chain’s he heard Ja‘far ibn ‘Awn is preserved without changing it to I heard. Abu al-‘Umays related to us and Qays informed us remain distinct reporting forms.

The quoted Qur’anic passage corresponds to 5:3, checked at https://quran.com/5/3. Only the excerpt present in the selected report is rendered. The festival, location at ‘Arafah and Friday are retained without importing explanatory pilgrimage parentheses.

segments.arabic: [46] حدثنا إسماعيل قال: حدثني مالك بن أنس عن عمه أبي سهيل بن مالك عن أبيه أنه سمع طلحة بن عبيد الله يقول
segments.english: Isma‘il related to us. He said: Malik ibn Anas related to me, from his uncle Abu Suhayl ibn Malik, from his father, that he heard Talhah ibn ‘Ubaydullah say:

segments.arabic: جاء رجل إلى رسول الله ﷺ من أهل نجد ثائر الرأس يسمع دوي صوته ولا يُفقه ما يقول حتى دنا فإذا هو يسأل عن الإسلام، فقال رسول الله ﷺ:
segments.english: A man from the people of Najd came to the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, with dishevelled hair. The sound of his voice could be heard, but what he was saying could not be understood, until he drew near. He was asking about Islam. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

segments.arabic: خمس صلوات في اليوم والليلة، فقال هل علي غيرها قال لا إلا أن تطوع قال رسول الله ﷺ: وصيام رمضان قال هل علي غيره قال لا إلا أن تطوع
segments.english: “Five prayers in the day and night.” He said: “Is anything else required of me?” He said: “No, unless you do so voluntarily.” The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “And fasting Ramadan.” He said: “Is anything else required of me?” He said: “No, unless you do so voluntarily.”

segments.arabic: قال وذكر له رسول الله ﷺ الزكاة قال هل علي غيرها قال لا إلا أن تطوع قال: فأدبر الرجل وهو يقول والله لا أزيد على هذا ولا أنقص قال رسول الله ﷺ: أفلح إن صدق
segments.english: He said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, mentioned zakat to him. He said: “Is anything else required of me?” He said: “No, unless you do so voluntarily.” He said: The man turned away saying: “By Allah, I will add nothing to this and take nothing away.” The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “He has succeeded, if he is truthful.”

notes: The opening description of the man is part of the report, not hidden inside the expandable chain. The complete route through Malik’s uncle, his father and Talhah is retained.

All three questions and voluntary-action exceptions remain. The source’s final success statement is not expanded into a promise of Paradise taken from comparator commentary. The selected day and night wording is retained.

segments.arabic: [47] حدثنا أحمد بن عبد الله بن علي المنجوفي قال: حدثنا روح قال: حدثنا عوف عن الحسن ومحمد عن أبي هريرة أن رسول الله ﷺ قال:
segments.english: Ahmad ibn ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Ali al-Manjufi related to us. He said: Rawh related to us. He said: ‘Awf related to us, from al-Hasan and Muhammad, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

segments.arabic: من اتبع جنازة مسلم إيمانا واحتسابا وكان معه حتى يصلي عليها ويفرغ من دفنها فإنه يرجع من الأجر بقيراطين كل قيراط مثل أحد ومن صلى عليها ثم رجع قبل أن تدفن فإنه يرجع بقيراط
segments.english: “Whoever follows a Muslim’s funeral with faith and seeking reward, and stays with it until the prayer over it is performed and its burial is finished, returns with two qirats of reward, each qirat like Uhud. Whoever prays over it, then returns before it is buried, returns with one qirat.”

segments.arabic: تابعه عثمان المؤذن قال: حدثنا عوف عن محمد عن أبي هريرة عن النبي ﷺ نحوه
segments.english: ‘Uthman the caller to prayer also transmitted it. He said: ‘Awf related to us, from Muhammad, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, with similar wording.

notes: The full Ahmad ibn ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Ali al-Manjufi chain and ‘Uthman the caller to prayer’s closing route remain. Bewley shortens the latter to ‘Uthman’s corroboration; the Khan-family report omits it.

Qirat and Uhud are retained rather than converted to a modern unit or an added explanatory sentence. The selected digital and modern print use معه; the historical print uses معها. The working English with it does not silently change the selected Arabic.

segments.arabic: [48] حدثنا محمد بن عرعرة قال: حدثنا شعبة عن زبيد قال: سألت أبا وائل عن المرجئة، فقال: حدثني عبد الله
segments.english: Muhammad ibn ‘Ar‘arah related to us. He said: Shu‘bah related to us, from Zubayd, who said: I asked Abu Wa’il about the Murji’ah. He said: ‘Abdullah related to me

segments.arabic: أن النبي ﷺ قال: سباب المسلم فسوق وقتاله كفر
segments.english: That the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “Insulting a Muslim is wrongdoing, and fighting him is disbelief.”

notes: The question to Abu Wa’il about the Murji’ah remains in the complete narrator introduction; no explanation of that group is inserted into the narration.
The selected fighting clause is rendered fighting him, without changing it to killing him as in the English comparison wording. Independent contextual review of the report’s terms remains pending.

Khan-family 1.2.46 contains two reports in one numbered record. This entry matches the first report; selected Hadith 49 matches the second. They remain distinct entries and full chains in this reader.

segments.arabic: [49] أخبرنا قتيبة بن سعيد حدثنا إسماعيل بن جعفر عن حميد عن أنس قال: أخبرني عبادة بن الصامت:
segments.english: Qutaybah ibn Sa‘id informed us. Isma‘il ibn Ja‘far related to us, from Humayd, from Anas, who said: ‘Ubadah ibn al-Samit informed me:

segments.arabic: أن رسول الله ﷺ خرج يخبر بليلة القدر فتلاحى رجلان من المسلمين، فقال إني خرجت لأخبركم بليلة القدر وإنه تلاحى فلان وفلان فرفعت وعسى أن يكون خيرا لكم التمسوها في السبع والتسع والخمس
segments.english: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, came out to tell about the Night of Decree, but two Muslim men quarrelled. He said: “I came out to tell you about the Night of Decree, but so-and-so and so-and-so quarrelled, and it was taken away. Perhaps that will be better for you. Seek it on the seventh, ninth and fifth.”

notes: Khan-family 1.2.46 contains both selected Hadith 48 and 49. This entry matches its second report, not a new one-number offset.
The selected digital and modern print begin Qutaybah informed us; the historical print has related to us. The selected reporting form is preserved.

The selected Arabic has it was taken away without an explicit noun for knowledge, and the seventh, ninth and fifth without expanded calendar dates. Those compressed expressions are retained; the English comparators supply explanatory knowledge/date wording. Their fuller explanations remain comparison evidence, not inserted source words. Qualified contextual review is pending.

segments.arabic: [50] حدثنا مسدد قال: حدثنا إسماعيل بن إبراهيم أخبرنا أبو حيان التيمي عن أبي زرعة عن أبي هريرة قال:
segments.english: Musaddad related to us. He said: Isma‘il ibn Ibrahim related to us. Abu Hayyan al-Taymi informed us, from Abu Zur‘ah, from Abu Hurayrah, who said:

segments.arabic: كان النبي ﷺ بارزا يوما للناس فأتاه جبريل، فقال: ما الإيمان قال أن تؤمن بالله وملائكته وبلقائه ورسله وتؤمن بالبعث
segments.english: One day the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was out before the people. Jibril came to him and said: “What is faith?” He said: “That you believe in Allah, His angels, meeting Him and His messengers, and believe in the resurrection.”

segments.arabic: قال: ما الإسلام قال الإسلام أن تعبد الله ولا تشرك به وتقيم الصلاة وتؤدي الزكاة المفروضة وتصوم رمضان
segments.english: He said: “What is Islam?” He said: “Islam is that you worship Allah and associate no partner with Him, establish prayer, give the obligatory zakat and fast Ramadan.”

segments.arabic: قال: ما الإحسان قال أن تعبد الله كأنك تراه فإن لم تكن تراه فإنه يراك
segments.english: He said: “What is ihsan?” He said: “That you worship Allah as though you see Him; if you do not see Him, He sees you.”

segments.arabic: قال متى الساعة قال: ما المسؤول عنها بأعلم من السائل وسأخبرك عن أشراطها إذا ولدت الأمة ربها وإذا تطاول رعاة الإبل البهم في البنيان في خمس لا يعلمهن إلا الله
segments.english: He said: “When is the Hour?” He said: “The one asked about it knows no more than the one asking. I will tell you about its signs: when a slave woman gives birth to her master, and when the herdsmen of black camels compete in the height of buildings. It is among five things that none knows except Allah.”

segments.arabic: ثم تلا النبي ﷺ { إن الله عنده علم الساعة } الآية ثم أدبر، فقال ردوه فلم يروا شيئا، فقال هذا جبريل جاء يعلم الناس دينهم
segments.english: Then the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, recited the verse: {Indeed, Allah has knowledge of the Hour}. Then he turned away. He said: “Bring him back.” They saw no one. He said: “This was Jibril. He came to teach the people their religion.”

segments.arabic: قال أبو عبد الله جعل ذلك كله من الإيمان
segments.english: Abu ‘Abdullah said: He made all of that part of faith.

notes: At the visitor’s arrival, the selected digital source explicitly says Jibril. Both inspected Arabic prints say a man there. The selected Arabic is retained and a separate on-screen discrepancy notice points to both witnesses. This remains unresolved for production.

The digital answer to the first question begins that you believe; both prints repeat faith before that phrase. No extra opening word is silently imported. Ihsan is retained as a term whose description follows in the report.

The questions, the two signs and the reference to five things known only to Allah remain. The selected text quotes only the opening of 31:34 and then says the verse; the complete Qur’anic verse is not inserted. Its Arabic location was checked at https://quran.com/31/34.
The final Abu ‘Abdullah observation is retained as a separate transmission note. The pronouns in the account are not replaced with additional speaker names absent from the selected Arabic.

segments.arabic: [51] حدثنا إبراهيم بن حمزة قال: حدثنا إبراهيم بن سعد عن صالح عن ابن شهاب عن عبيد الله بن عبد الله أن عبد الله بن عباس أخبره قال: أخبرني أبو سفيان:
segments.english: Ibrahim ibn Hamzah related to us. He said: Ibrahim ibn Sa‘d related to us, from Salih, from Ibn Shihab, from ‘Ubaydullah ibn ‘Abdullah, that ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Abbas informed him. He said: Abu Sufyan informed me:

segments.arabic: أن هرقل قال له سألتك هل يزيدون أم ينقصون فزعمت أنهم يزيدون وكذلك الإيمان حتى يتم وسألتك هل يرتد أحد سخطة لدينه بعد أن يدخل فيه فزعمت أن لا وكذلك الإيمان حين تخالط بشاشته القلوب لا يسخطه أحد
segments.english: Heraclius said to him: “I asked you whether they increase or decrease, and you reported that they increase. Such is faith until it becomes complete. I asked you whether anyone turns back, displeased with his religion after entering it, and you reported that no one does. Such is faith when its joy mingles with hearts: no one is displeased with it.”

notes: This report remains a separate narration with its own complete chain, even though it overlaps the longer Heraclius report in Hadith 7. It is not deduplicated or replaced by a link.
Both English comparisons preserve the two questions and the statements about faith. The shorter source heading is simply Chapter; no topic title has been invented.

segments.arabic: [52] حدثنا أبو نعيم حدثنا زكريا عن عامر قال: سمعت النعمان بن بشير يقول: سمعت رسول الله ﷺ يقول:
segments.english: Abu Nu‘aym related to us. Zakariyya related to us, from ‘Amir, who said: I heard al-Nu‘man ibn Bashir say: I heard the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, say:

segments.arabic: الحلال بين والحرام بين وبينهما مشبهات لا يعلمها كثير من الناس فمن اتقي المشبهات استبرأ لدينه وعرضه ومن وقع في الشبهات كراع يرعى حول الحمى يوشك أن يواقعه ألا وإن لكل ملك حمى ألا إن حمى الله في أرضه محارمه
segments.english: “What is lawful is clear, and what is forbidden is clear. Between them are doubtful matters that many people do not know. Whoever avoids the doubtful matters safeguards his religion and his honour. Whoever falls into doubtful matters is like a herdsman grazing around a protected pasture, close to entering it. Indeed, every king has a protected pasture. Indeed, Allah’s protected pasture on His earth is what He has forbidden.

segments.arabic: ألا وإن في الجسد مضغة إذا صلحت صلح الجسد كله وإذا فسدت فسد الجسد كله ألا وهي القلب
segments.english: “Indeed, in the body is a piece of flesh: if it is sound, the entire body is sound; if it is corrupt, the entire body is corrupt. Indeed, it is the heart.”

notes: The selected lawful/forbidden contrast, doubtful matters, protected-pasture comparison and final heart passage are all retained. Many people is kept for كثير من الناس rather than the comparators’ most people.

The historical print begins the report with an additional إن. The selected digital and modern print begin الحلال; the selected wording is unchanged. No legal examples or rulings are added to the metaphor.

segments.arabic: [53] حدثنا علي بن الجعد قال: أخبرنا شعبة عن أبي جمرة قال:
segments.english: ‘Ali ibn al-Ja‘d related to us. He said: Shu‘bah informed us, from Abu Jamrah, who said:

segments.arabic: كنت أقعد مع ابن عباس يجلسني على سريره، فقال أقم عندي حتى أجعل لك سهما من مالي فأقمت معه شهرين،
segments.english: I used to sit with Ibn ‘Abbas, and he would seat me on his bed. He said: “Stay with me until I assign you a share of my wealth.” So I stayed with him for two months.

segments.arabic: ثم قال إن وفد عبد القيس لما أتوا النبي ﷺ قال: من القوم أو من الوفد قالوا ربيعة قال مرحبا بالقوم أو بالوفد غير خزايا ولا ندامى فقالوا يا رسول الله إنا لا نستطيع أن نأتيك إلا في شهر الحرام وبيننا وبينك هذا الحي من كفار مضر فمرنا بأمر فصل نخبر به من وراءنا وندخل به الجنة
segments.english: Then he said: When the delegation of ‘Abd al-Qays came to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, he said: “Who are the people—or the delegation?” They said: “Rabi‘ah.” He said: “Welcome to the people—or the delegation—without disgrace or regret.” They said: “Messenger of Allah, we cannot come to you except in the sacred month. Between us and you is this clan of the unbelievers of Mudar. Give us a decisive instruction that we can tell those we have left behind and by which we may enter the Garden.”

segments.arabic: وسألوه عن الأشربة فأمرهم بأربع ونهاهم عن أربع أمرهم بالإيمان بالله وحده قال أتدرون ما الإيمان بالله وحده قالوا الله ورسوله أعلم قال شهادة أن لا إله إلا الله وأن محمدا رسول الله وإقام الصلاة وإيتاء الزكاة وصيام رمضان وأن تعطوا من المغنم الخمس
segments.english: They asked him about drinks. He commanded them to do four things and forbade them four things. He commanded them to believe in Allah alone. He said: “Do you know what faith in Allah alone is?” They said: “Allah and His Messenger know best.” He said: “Testifying that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, establishing prayer, giving zakat, fasting Ramadan, and giving one fifth of the spoils.”

segments.arabic: ونهاهم عن أربع عن الحنتم والدباء والنقير والمزفت وربما قال المقير، وقال احفظوهن وأخبروا بهن من وراءكم
segments.english: He forbade them four things: al-hantam, al-dubba’, al-naqir and al-muzaffat—and sometimes he said al-muqayyar. He said: “Remember them, and tell them to those you have left behind.”

notes: The full opening account of Abu Jamrah’s two-month stay with Ibn ‘Abbas remains part of the visible report. Both occurrences of uncertainty between people and delegation remain.

The Arabic says four commands and then gives the clauses as selected, including the fifth of the spoils. The working translation preserves that wording and order without inventing a new numbered list or correcting the reported count.

The names al-hantam, al-dubba’, al-naqir, al-muzaffat and the alternative al-muqayyar are retained. The English comparisons add explanations of drinking vessels; these explanations are not presented as explicit words of the selected narration. Their terminology and context need independent review.
The selected digital phrase is في شهر الحرام where both print witnesses have في الشهر الحرام. The selected Arabic remains unchanged; the working English renders the sacred month.

segments.arabic: [54] حدثنا عبد الله بن مسلمة قال: أخبرنا مالك عن يحيى بن سعيد عن محمد بن إبراهيم عن علقمة بن وقاص عن عمر أن رسول الله ﷺ قال:
segments.english: ‘Abdullah ibn Maslamah related to us. He said: Malik informed us, from Yahya ibn Sa‘id, from Muhammad ibn Ibrahim, from ‘Alqamah ibn Waqqas, from ‘Umar, that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

segments.arabic: الأعمال بالنية ولكل امرئ ما نوى فمن كانت هجرته إلى الله ورسوله فهجرته إلى الله ورسوله ومن كانت هجرته لدنيا يصيبها أو امرأة يتزوجها فهجرته إلى ما هاجر إليه
segments.english: “Actions are by intention, and each person has what he intended. Whoever’s migration is to Allah and His Messenger, his migration is to Allah and His Messenger. Whoever’s migration is for worldly gain he obtains or a woman he marries, his migration is to what he migrated to.”

notes: This intention report is kept distinct from Hadith 1. It explicitly includes the migration-to-Allah-and-His-Messenger clause and its repetition, which are not replaced by another occurrence’s wording.

The historical print uses Malik related to us; the selected digital source and modern print use Malik informed us. The selected form is retained. No explanatory reward clause is inserted into the opening statement.

segments.arabic: [55] حدثنا حجاج بن منهال قال: حدثنا شعبة قال: أخبرني عدي بن ثابت قال: سمعت عبد الله بن يزيد عن أبي مسعود عن النبي ﷺ قال:
segments.english: Hajjaj ibn Minhal related to us. He said: Shu‘bah related to us. He said: ‘Adi ibn Thabit informed me. He said: I heard ‘Abdullah ibn Yazid report from Abu Mas‘ud, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, who said:

segments.arabic: إذا أنفق الرجل على أهله يحتسبها فهو له صدقة
segments.english: “When a man spends on his family seeking reward for it, it is charity for him.”

notes: The source has the whole chain and report in a single paragraph with a newline. The exact paragraph is retained; separate presentation spans make the chain expandable without losing or rewriting the report.
‘Adi informed me and I heard ‘Abdullah ibn Yazid remain distinct from the plural opening related to us forms. The seeking-reward clause remains within the report.

segments.arabic: [56] حدثنا الحكم بن نافع قال: أخبرنا شعيب عن الزهري قال: حدثني عامر بن سعد عن سعد بن أبي وقاص أنه أخبره أن رسول الله ﷺ قال:
segments.english: Al-Hakam ibn Nafi‘ related to us. He said: Shu‘ayb informed us, from al-Zuhri, who said: ‘Amir ibn Sa‘d related to me, from Sa‘d ibn Abi Waqqas, who informed him that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

segments.arabic: إنك لن تنفق نفقة تبتغي بها وجه الله إلا أجرت عليها حتى ما تجعل في في امرأتك
segments.english: “Indeed, you will be rewarded for any spending by which you seek Allah’s Face, even what you put into your wife’s mouth.”

notes: The source’s وجه الله is provisionally rendered Allah’s Face. The English comparisons use a for-Allah’s-sake rendering. No theological explanation is inserted, and independent review remains pending.

The selected في في امرأتك is preserved exactly. The English renders what you put into your wife’s mouth; no additional morsel word is imported from a comparator. Nor is all spending narrowed to spending on family as in the Bewley wording.

segments.arabic: [57] حدثنا مسدد قال: حدثنا يحيى عن إسماعيل قال: حدثني قيس بن أبي حازم عن جرير بن عبد الله قال:
segments.english: Musaddad related to us. He said: Yahya related to us, from Isma‘il, who said: Qays ibn Abi Hazim related to me, from Jarir ibn ‘Abdullah, who said:

segments.arabic: بايعت رسول الله ﷺ على إقام الصلاة وإيتاء الزكاة والنصح لكل مسلم.
segments.english: I pledged allegiance to the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, to establish prayer, give zakat and be sincere toward every Muslim.

notes: The selected Arabic and both print witnesses name Jarir ibn ‘Abdullah. The Bewley page at entry 57 reverses the name to ‘Abdullah ibn Jarir; that comparator reading is not imported.
All three commitments remain in order. Nush is provisionally rendered sincerity toward every Muslim, consistent with the following report; no added behavioural examples are supplied.

segments.arabic: [58] حدثنا أبو النعمان قال: حدثنا أبو عوانة عن زياد بن علاقة قال:
segments.english: Abu al-Nu‘man related to us. He said: Abu ‘Awanah related to us, from Ziyad ibn ‘Ilaqah, who said:

segments.arabic: سمعت جرير بن عبد الله يقول يوم مات المغيرة بن شعبة قام فحمد الله وأثنى عليه، وقال عليكم باتقاء الله وحده لا شريك له والوقار والسكينة حتى يأتيكم أمير فإنما يأتيكم الآن، ثم قال استعفوا لأميركم فإنه كان يحب العفو،
segments.english: I heard Jarir ibn ‘Abdullah speak on the day al-Mughirah ibn Shu‘bah died. He stood, praised Allah and extolled Him, and said: “You must fear Allah alone, who has no partner, and maintain dignity and calm until a leader comes to you, for he will come to you shortly.” Then he said: “Ask pardon for your leader, for he loved pardon.”

segments.arabic: ثم قال: أما بعد فإني أتيت النبي ﷺ قلت: أبايعك على الإسلام فشرط علي والنصح لكل مسلم فبايعته على هذا ورب هذا المسجد إني لناصح لكم ثم استغفر ونزل.
segments.english: Then he said: “Now then, I came to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and said: ‘I pledge allegiance to you upon Islam.’ He stipulated for me: ‘And sincerity toward every Muslim.’ So I pledged allegiance to him on this. By the Lord of this mosque, I am sincere toward you.” Then he sought forgiveness and came down.

notes: The date context, praise of Allah, call for dignity and calm, request for pardon, pledge condition, oath and closing descent are retained. This is Jarir’s address with an embedded report of his pledge; the entire speech is not attributed directly to the Prophet.

The selected source asks pardon for your leader without an inserted late qualifier. The Prophet’s condition retains the conjunction And sincerity toward every Muslim. No unprinted pledge conditions are supplied.
